title: Move It to the Thread
goal: The thread may outlive main. Hand it the String correctly, without cloning.

choices.text: { let copy = name.clone(); move || println!("hello from {copy}") }

hints: spawn demands 'static: the closure may run after main's frame is gone, so it can't borrow name (E0373).
main never uses name afterwards - just give it away with move. The clone buys nothing.
explanation: A spawned thread's closure must be 'static: the thread might outlive the function that made it, so borrowing name is rejected with E0373 ('closure may outlive the current function'). `move` transfers the String into the closure - ownership crosses the thread boundary, no lifetime to violate. The clone-then-move variant also satisfies 'static but pays an allocation to keep a name main never touches again. When the data's last user is the thread, moving IS the clean answer.
